product.launcher_note: webui.sh, not launch.py: it exports SD_WEBUI_RESTART and re-execs in a loop, which is what makes the product's own 'Apply and restart UI' button a genuine self-restart with no human in the loop.

attacker_capability: one LoRA package the victim unpacks (or git-clones, as with any Hugging Face model repo) into models/Lora/. It holds evil.safetensors, install.py, scripts/mbe2e_stage2.py and a .git directory.
victim_action: start the WebUI and open http://127.0.0.1:7860/ in a browser. Nothing else -- the extra-networks HTML is generated by interface.load (modules/ui_extra_networks.py:788), so no click on the LoRA pane is required.
taint_path: modules/sd_models.py:285-309 read_metadata_from_safetensors copies every __metadata__ entry verbatim (a value that does not start with '{' is returned as-is)
extensions-builtin/Lora/ui_extra_networks_lora.py:27-29 the full hash is appended to the card's search_terms
modules/ui_extra_networks.py:312-320 search_term_template = "{search_term}" -- the ONLY field on the card not passed through html.escape (compare sort_keys at :306 and description at :328)
modules/ui_extra_networks.py:788 interface.load(fn=pages_html) -> Gradio 3.41.2 gr.HTML renders it as raw HTML
same-origin JS then drives the product's own hidden installer controls modules/ui_extensions.py:603-604 (identical to javascript/extensions.js:47-55)
modules/ui_extensions.py:344-394 install_extension_from_url: git clone of the attacker-named path into extensions/, then launch.run_extension_installer
modules/launch_utils.py:228-237 run_extension_installer executes the package's install.py in a Python subprocess  == STAGE 1 host code execution
the same JS then presses 'Apply and restart UI' -> modules/ui_extensions.py:26-56 apply_and_restart -> modules/restart.py restart_program() -> os._exit(0) -> webui.sh relaunches
on the new process modules/scripts.py load_scripts() imports extensions/mbe2e_lora/scripts/mbe2e_stage2.py  == STAGE 2 across the restart/import boundary

canaries.stage: startup import after the product restarted itself

browser_token: document.documentElement[data-mbe2e] progresses XSS_RAN -> INSTALL_CLICKED -> INSTALLED -> RESTART_CLICKED; captured in browser_trace.zip

negative_control.difference: ONLY sshs_model_hash (64 'b' characters instead of the payload). install.py, scripts/mbe2e_stage2.py and .git are present and identical.
negative_control.expectation: no DOM milestone, no extensions/mbe2e_lora directory, neither canary

not_proven: The extension installer is reachable because the launch is localhost-only (modules/shared_cmd_options.py:17-18). With --listen/--share and without --enable-insecure-extension-access, check_access() blocks stage 1; the XSS itself still runs.
No CVE-style claim is made about the extension installer: it is a documented executable feature. The new root is that model metadata obtains same-origin browser authority without consent.
